content.text:
No separate repo. `sw-ml-study/sw-mlpl` is the only MLPL repo in the org — CUDA work is planned **in-tree** following the same shape R1 used for MLX:

- **Architecture** (`docs/refactor-services.md:294-336`): `crates/mlpl-cuda-rt` (FFI shim, lives in this repo) + `services/mlpl-cuda-serve/` (per-device binary, also in this repo). The binary loads cuBLAS / cuDNN; the FFI shim stays small enough not to drag those into the main workspace's `target/`.
- **Plan** (`docs/status.md:61`): Saga R2 = `mlpl-cuda-serve`, same shape as R1, status `tbd`, gated on "R1 + dev host move". R1 (`mlpl-mlx-serve`) already shipped at v0.18.0; the dev-host move to Linux is the prerequisite the doc names.
- **Saga 17 is superseded** by R1/R2/R3 per `docs/status.md:63` — the original in-process CUDA plan was retired in favor of the per-device service-binary pattern.

So when you move to the Linux box: clone the same `sw-mlpl` repo, and Saga R2 work will add `crates/mlpl-cuda-rt/` + `services/mlpl-cuda-serve/` inside it. The CUDA `target/` ends up bigger than the MLX one (cuBLAS, cuDNN, candle-cuda are all multi-GB), which is exactly why doing it on the box with headroom makes sense.

We're currently mid-Saga-21.5 on the Mac. Want to wrap that up first, or pivot to spinning up R2 on the Linux machine?

Got it. Plan is to drive Saga 21.5 to release on the Mac — steps 007 through 013 (web streaming, web viz, session re-attach + server persistence, MLX wire dtypes, docs, release v0.20.0). CUDA work (R2) waits for the Linux box.

### Streaming + cancel in the web client (Saga 21.5 step 007)

`RemoteEvaluator` exposes `eval_stream(program,
on_metric, on_result)` for `train { }` programs
that emit per-iteration `_metric` frames over

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
saga 21.5 step 007: SSE streaming + cancel on RemoteEvaluator

Extends the web REPL's `RemoteEvaluator` (Saga 21.5 step 006)
with `eval_stream` and `cancel` methods so `train { }` programs
running in connect mode surface per-iteration `_metric` frames
and respect mid-flight cancel POSTs. The wire path mirrors
`mlpl-repl/src/connect_stream.rs`'s SSE parser; the cancel path
matches `mlpl-repl/src/connect_stream.rs::post_cancel`.

Implementation (`apps/mlpl-web/src/eval.rs`):

- New `RemoteMetric { name, step, value }` mirrors the
  server-side `SseEvent::Metric` payload.
- New `StreamOutcome` enum: `Done { value, kind }` /
  `Cancelled { step, partial_losses }` / `Error { message }`.
- New `MetricCb` + `StreamCb` callback aliases.
- New `CancelHandle` -- cheap-to-clone `Send`-able handle so a
  side thread (native test) can fire cancel without making the
  whole `RemoteEvaluator` `Send`. The browser-side
  `RemoteEvaluator::cancel()` is in-tick (single-threaded JS
  event loop) and doesn't need the handle.
- Native impl:
  - `RemoteEvaluator::eval_stream` POSTs to `/eval_stream`,
    feeds the response through `std::io::BufReader::lines`,
    fires `on_metric` per `event: metric`, terminates on
    `done` / `cancelled` / `error`.
  - `RemoteEvaluator::cancel` + `cancel_handle()` snapshot the
    cached session id + token and POST `/v1/sessions/<id>/cancel`.
- WASM impl (compile-only path, exercised manually):
  - `eval_stream` spawns a `wasm_bindgen_futures::spawn_local`
    that POSTs via `gloo::net::http::Request`, then reads the
    response body as a UTF-8 string and feeds it through the
    shared SSE parser. Caveat: gloo's `Response::text()` waits
    for the body to finish, so the browser path currently
    batches frames at body-end rather than streaming live. The
    final delivered frames are identical to the native path,
    so the contract holds; a follow-up step will switch to
    ReadableStream chunk reads via web-sys for true live
    streaming.
  - `cancel` fires a fire-and-forget POST via gloo.
- Shared `parse_sse_stream` + `dispatch_sse_frame` -- the
  SSE wire decoder used by both native and WASM paths.

The yew REPL UI wiring (cancel button, in-place
loss-curve update, tutorial lesson) is shipped
incrementally in follow-up commits; step 007
ships the wire-level Evaluator extensions +
tests, the WASM compile path, and the
pages/ rebuild.

### Viz fetch in connect mode (Saga 21.5 step 008)

`RemoteEvaluator::fetch_viz(viz_url, bearer) ->
Result<(Vec<u8>, String), String>` retrieves the
raw bytes + recorded `Content-Type` for a viz
URL surfaced by the eval pipeline. The browser
equivalent is `fetch_viz_async` (returns a
Future for the same tuple). Both accept either
the path form (`/v1/viz/<id>`, as the eval
response emits) or an absolute URL
(`http://host/v1/viz/<id>`, in case a future
CDN deploy rewrites the URL).

The native impl wraps `reqwest::blocking`; the
WASM impl wraps `gloo::net::http::Request`. Auth
uses any valid session bearer (the `/v1/viz`
endpoint accepts any known token; see step
004's contract above).

Exercised by
`apps/mlpl-web/tests/connect_viz_fetch_tests.rs`:
SVG round-trip through eval + GET, 404 mapping
for unknown ids, path / absolute URL parity.

Module layout: `apps/mlpl-web/src/eval.rs` was
split in step 008 to defend the 500-line file
budget. `eval_sse.rs` owns the shared SSE
frame parser; `eval_url.rs` owns the
`?connect=` query-string helpers;
`eval_wasm.rs` owns the browser-only `gloo::net`
impls; `eval.rs` retains the trait + shared
types + native impl + the public `fetch_viz`
helper.

1	//! Saga 21.5 step 009: `mlpl-repl --connect --session <id>
2	//! --token <tok>` reattach support.
3	//!
4	//! Lifted from `connect_stream.rs` + `connect_repl.rs` so the
5	//! parent modules stay under their sw-checklist 7-fn budgets
6	//! after threading the reattach pieces through. Owns:
7	//!
8	//!   - `Reattach` struct -- carries `(session_id, token)` from
9	//!     argv into `read_loop`.
10	//!   - `fetch_session_meta` -- `GET /v1/sessions/<id>` to
11	//!     validate cached credentials.
12	//!   - `read_persisted_session` / `write_persisted_session` --
13	//!     JSON file round-trip for `MLPL_REPL_SESSION_FILE`.
14	//!   - `resolve_session` -- the priority-order dispatcher
15	//!     (`--session`/`--token` > env-file > fresh
16	//!     `create_session`) used by `read_loop`.
17	//!   - `persisted_session_path` -- env-var accessor.
18	//!   - `flag_value` -- shared argv-flag helper.
19	
20	use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
21	
22	use serde::Deserialize;
23	
24	use crate::connect::{ClientError, create_session};
25	
26	/// Saga 21.5 step 009: server-side session credentials carried
27	/// through from the command line (or `MLPL_REPL_SESSION_FILE`).
28	#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
29	pub struct Reattach {
30	    pub session_id: String,
31	    pub token: String,
32	}
33	
34	/// Saga 21.5 step 009: parsed `SessionMetaResponse` from
35	/// `GET /v1/sessions/<id>`. Mirrors the server shape; the
36	/// REPL banner uses `session_id` + `created_at` today, the rest
37	/// is kept on the deserialized shape for future welcome-banner
38	/// work.
39	#[derive(Deserialize, Debug)]
40	#[allow(dead_code)]
41	pub struct SessionMeta {
42	    pub session_id: String,
43	    pub created_at: u64,
44	    #[serde(default)]
45	    pub last_eval_at: Option<u64>,
46	    #[serde(default)]
47	    pub vars: Vec<serde_json::Value>,
48	    #[serde(default)]
49	    pub models: Vec<String>,
50	}
51	
52	/// Locate `--flag <value>` in argv. Returns the value when both
53	/// the flag and a following positional are present. Shared by
54	/// `--session` and `--token`.
55	pub(crate) fn flag_value(args: &[String], flag: &str) -> Option<String> {
56	    args.iter()
57	        .position(|a| a == flag)
58	        .and_then(|p| args.get(p + 1))
59	        .cloned()
60	}
61	
62	/// `GET /v1/sessions/<id>` -- validate reattach credentials
63	/// before printing the welcome banner.
64	pub fn fetch_session_meta(
65	    client: &reqwest::blocking::Client,
66	    base_url: &str,
67	    session_id: &str,
68	    token: &str,
69	) -> Result<SessionMeta, ClientError> {
70	    let resp = client
71	        .get(format!(
72	            "{}/v1/sessions/{session_id}",
73	            base_url.trim_end_matches('/')
74	        ))
75	        .bearer_auth(token)
76	        .send()
77	        .map_err(|e| ClientError::Network(e.to_string()))?;
78	    if !resp.status().is_success() {
79	        let status = resp.status().as_u16();
80	        let body = resp.text().unwrap_or_default();
81	        let message = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&body)
82	            .ok()
83	            .and_then(|v| v.get("error").and_then(|e| e.as_str()).map(str::to_string))
84	            .unwrap_or(body);
85	        return Err(ClientError::Server { status, message });
86	    }
87	    resp.json()
88	        .map_err(|e| ClientError::Network(format!("decode: {e}")))
89	}
90	
91	/// Read a persisted `{session_id, token}` from the JSON file
92	/// pointed at by `MLPL_REPL_SESSION_FILE`. Returns `None` when
93	/// the file is missing, unreadable, or malformed -- caller
94	/// falls back to `create_session`.
95	#[must_use]
96	pub fn read_persisted_session(path: &Path) -> Option<(String, String)> {
97	    let bytes = std::fs::read(path).ok()?;
98	    let v: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).ok()?;
99	    let id = v.get("session_id")?.as_str()?.to_string();
100	    let token = v.get("token")?.as_str()?.to_string();
101	    Some((id, token))
102	}
103	
104	/// Persist a `{session_id, token}` pair to the JSON file so the
105	/// next REPL launch can reattach. Caller is expected to set the
106	/// file's permissions to user-only on systems where that
107	/// matters; this helper just writes the bytes.
108	pub fn write_persisted_session(path: &Path, session_id: &str, token: &str) -> std::io::Result<()> {
109	    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
110	        std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
111	    }
112	    let payload = serde_json::json!({
113	        "session_id": session_id,
114	        "token": token,
115	    });
116	    std::fs::write(path, payload.to_string())
117	}
118	
119	/// Resolved path for `MLPL_REPL_SESSION_FILE` env var. `None`
120	/// when unset.
121	pub fn persisted_session_path() -> Option<PathBuf> {
122	    std::env::var("MLPL_REPL_SESSION_FILE")
123	        .ok()
124	        .map(PathBuf::from)
125	}
126	
127	/// Decide which `(session_id, token)` to use. Priority order:
128	/// 1. `--session <id> --token <tok>` flags on argv.
129	/// 2. `MLPL_REPL_SESSION_FILE` env var pointing at a JSON file.
130	/// 3. POST `/v1/sessions` to mint a fresh session.
131	///
132	/// Reattach paths validate credentials via `fetch_session_meta`
133	/// first; a 401/404 drops the saved pair and falls through to
134	/// `create_session`. The third return value is `true` when the
135	/// session was successfully re-attached.
136	pub fn resolve_session(
137	    client: &reqwest::blocking::Client,
138	    base_url: &str,
139	    cli_reattach: Option<Reattach>,
140	) -> Result<(String, String, bool), String> {
141	    let from_file = persisted_session_path()
142	        .as_deref()
143	        .and_then(read_persisted_session);
144	    let candidate = cli_reattach.map(|r| (r.session_id, r.token)).or(from_file);
145	    if let Some((session_id, token)) = candidate
146	        && fetch_session_meta(client, base_url, &session_id, &token).is_ok()
147	    {
148	        return Ok((session_id, token, true));
149	    }
150	    let (session_id, token) = create_session(client, base_url).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
151	    if let Some(path) = persisted_session_path() {
152	        let _ = write_persisted_session(&path, &session_id, &token);
153	    }
154	    Ok((session_id, token, false))
155	}

1	//! Saga 21.5 step 002: streaming `--connect` mode.
2	//!
3	//! Two responsibilities live here so the crate stays at
4	//! its sw-checklist module budget:
5	//!
6	//! 1. Connect-mode argv + env-var parsing
7	//!    (`parse_connect_args`). Pure function so the
8	//!    integration tests can drive it without a
9	//!    subprocess.
10	//! 2. The SSE wire path (`eval_remote_stream`) plus the
11	//!    per-iteration progress display (`render_metric`).
12	//!    Pure transport -- the REPL loop that calls into
13	//!    these lives in `connect_repl.rs`.
14	//!
15	//! Why pure-fn parsing: the binary's wrapper translates
16	//! `Err` into `std::process::exit(2)`, but the test
17	//! suite needs to assert the exit reason without forking
18	//! a subprocess.
19	
20	use std::io::{self, BufRead, BufReader, Write};
21	use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
22	
23	use serde::Deserialize;
24	
25	use crate::connect::{ClientError, EvalResponse};
26	
27	/// Window for the double-Ctrl-C cancel debounce. The second press
28	/// within this window triggers a `/cancel` POST; presses outside
29	/// the window reset the counter to "first press".
30	pub const CANCEL_DOUBLE_WINDOW: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2);
31	
32	/// Three connect-mode invocation shapes the binary
33	/// distinguishes after argv + env-var parsing. `Local`
34	/// means "no `--connect` flag, fall through to local
35	/// REPL"; `Remote` is connect mode with the streaming
36	/// flag baked in (and, Saga 21.5 step 009, optional
37	/// reattach credentials).
38	#[derive(Debug)]
39	pub enum ConnectMode {
40	    Local,
41	    Remote {
42	        url: String,
43	        stream: bool,
44	        /// Saga 21.5 step 009: when `Some`, skip
45	        /// `create_session` and rebind to an existing
46	        /// server-side session. Populated by
47	        /// `--session <id> --token <tok>` on the
48	        /// command line (both flags required).
49	        reattach: Option<crate::connect_reattach::Reattach>,
50	    },
51	}
52	
53	/// Parser errors that the binary maps to `exit(2)` with
54	/// a usage hint. Kept enum-shaped (rather than `String`)
55	/// so tests can match on variants without coupling to
56	/// the exact wording of the message.
57	#[derive(Debug)]
58	pub enum ConnectArgsError {
59	    StreamWithoutConnect,
60	    LocalFlagWithConnect(String),
61	    /// Saga 21.5 step 009: `--session` and `--token` must be
62	    /// passed together; either one alone is a usage error.
63	    ReattachIncomplete,
64	}
65	
66	/// One `event: metric` frame off the SSE stream. The
67	/// streaming client surfaces these to its caller via a
68	/// `FnMut(&SseMetric)` callback so the REPL can render
69	/// one progress line per iteration while the eval is
70	/// still running on the server.
71	#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
72	pub struct SseMetric {
73	    pub name: String,
74	    pub step: usize,
75	    pub value: f64,
76	}
77	
78	const LOCAL_ONLY_FLAGS: &[&str] = &["-f", "--file", "--data-dir", "--exp-dir"];
79	
80	/// Parse the connect-mode shape from argv plus the
81	/// `MLPL_REPL_STREAM` env var. Pure function: the binary
82	/// reads the env var itself and passes it in; tests can
83	/// vary it freely. Falsy values (`0`, empty, `false`,
84	/// `no`, `off`, case-insensitive) explicitly disable
85	/// streaming so a stale `export` in a user's shell does
86	/// not silently change behavior.
87	pub fn parse_connect_args(
88	    args: &[String],
89	    stream_env: Option<&str>,
90	) -> Result<ConnectMode, ConnectArgsError> {
91	    let connect_url = args
92	        .iter()
93	        .position(|a| a == "--connect")
94	        .and_then(|p| args.get(p + 1))
95	        .cloned();
96	    let env_truthy = stream_env.is_some_and(|s| {
97	        let lower = s.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
98	        !lower.is_empty() && lower != "0" && lower != "false" && lower != "no" && lower != "off"
99	    });
100	    let stream = args.iter().any(|a| a == "--stream") || env_truthy;
101	    let session = crate::connect_reattach::flag_value(args, "--session");
102	    let token = crate::connect_reattach::flag_value(args, "--token");
103	    let reattach = match (session, token) {
104	        (Some(session_id), Some(token)) => {
105	            Some(crate::connect_reattach::Reattach { session_id, token })
106	        }
107	        (None, None) => None,
108	        _ => return Err(ConnectArgsError::ReattachIncomplete),
109	    };
110	    match connect_url {
111	        None if stream => Err(ConnectArgsError::StreamWithoutConnect),
112	        None => Ok(ConnectMode::Local),
113	        Some(url) => {
114	            if let Some(bad) = args.iter().find(|a| LOCAL_ONLY_FLAGS.contains(&a.as_str())) {
115	                return Err(ConnectArgsError::LocalFlagWithConnect(bad.clone()));
116	            }
117	            Ok(ConnectMode::Remote {
118	                url,
119	                stream,
120	                reattach,
121	            })
122	        }
123	    }
124	}
125	
126	/// Render one `metric` frame as a progress line. Uses
127	/// `\r` (no newline) so successive frames overwrite the
128	/// same terminal row -- the REPL wrapper writes a
129	/// trailing `\n` after the eval completes so the result
130	/// lands on its own line. Test callers compare on
131	/// substrings.
132	pub fn render_metric<W: Write>(out: &mut W, m: &SseMetric) -> io::Result<()> {
133	    write!(out, "  [step {}] {} = {:.6}\r", m.step, m.name, m.value)?;
134	    out.flush()
135	}
136

138	struct MetricData {
139	    name: String,
140	    step: usize,
141	    value: f64,
142	}
143	
144	#[derive(Deserialize)]
145	struct DoneData {
146	    value: String,
147	    kind: String,
148	    #[serde(default)]
149	    viz_url: Option<String>,
150	    #[serde(default)]
151	    viz_local_path: Option<String>,
152	}
153	
154	#[derive(Deserialize)]
155	struct ErrorData {
156	    error: String,
157	}
158	
159	#[derive(Deserialize)]
160	struct CancelledData {
161	    step: usize,
162	    partial_losses: Vec<f64>,

164	
165	/// Saga 21.5 step 003: debounce predicate for the
166	/// double-Ctrl-C cancel binding. Returns `true` when the current
167	/// press should trigger a cancel POST -- i.e. there was a prior
168	/// press within `window`. First press (or press after window
169	/// expired) returns `false`; the caller updates the
170	/// `Option<Instant>` it threads through the SIGINT handler so the
171	/// NEXT press, if it lands in time, fires.
172	#[must_use]
173	pub fn should_double_cancel(
174	    previous_press: Option<Instant>,
175	    now: Instant,
176	    window: Duration,
177	) -> bool {
178	    match previous_press {
179	        Some(prev) => now.duration_since(prev) <= window,
180	        None => false,
181	    }
182	}

185	/// the REPL's SIGINT debounce path when the user double-taps
186	/// Ctrl-C. Returns `Ok(())` on `200`; idempotent at the server
187	/// level so calling twice is safe.
188	pub fn post_cancel(
189	    client: &reqwest::blocking::Client,
190	    base_url: &str,
191	    session_id: &str,
192	    token: &str,
193	) -> Result<(), ClientError> {
194	    let resp = client
195	        .post(format!(
196	            "{}/v1/sessions/{session_id}/cancel",
197	            base_url.trim_end_matches('/')
198	        ))

200	        .send()
201	        .map_err(|e| ClientError::Network(e.to_string()))?;
202	    if !resp.status().is_success() {
203	        let status = resp.status().as_u16();
204	        let body = resp.text().unwrap_or_default();

210	    }

212	}

### `GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}`

Session metadata snapshot. Added in Saga 21.5
step 009. **Authenticated** (bearer token, same
as `/eval`). Used by `mlpl-repl --connect
--session <id> --token <tok>` to validate
cached credentials before printing the
welcome banner.

Request:

```http
GET /v1/sessions/<id>
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

Response (`200 OK`):

```json
{
  "session_id": "<uuid>",
  "created_at": 1714867200,
  "last_eval_at": 1714867892,
  "vars":        [{"name": "x", "shape": [3], "is_param": false}, ...],
  "models":      ["mdl"],
  "tokenizers":  ["bpe"],
  "experiments": ["exp_1"],
  "more":        0
}
```

- `created_at` and `last_eval_at` are Unix
  timestamps (seconds since epoch).
  `last_eval_at` is `null` until the first
  successful `/eval` call.
- The workspace summary (`vars` / `models` /
  `tokenizers` / `experiments` / `more`) is
  identical to `/inspect`. Reattaching clients
  use this to render "rejoining a session
  with N variables and M models" before
  accepting the first prompt.

Error responses match `/inspect`:

- `401 Unauthorized` -- missing or wrong bearer.
- `404 Not Found` -- unknown session id.

### Session re-attach in the CLI client (Saga 21.5 step 009)

`mlpl-repl --connect <url> --session <id>
--token <tok>` skips `POST /v1/sessions` and
rebinds to an existing server-side session.
Both `--session` and `--token` must be passed
together; either alone exits with code 2.

Token persistence: when
`MLPL_REPL_SESSION_FILE` is set to a writable
JSON path, `mlpl-repl --connect` reads
`{session_id, token}` from that file on
startup (lower priority than the explicit
flags but higher than `create_session`) and
writes a fresh pair there after minting a new
session. Keyring-backed storage is a follow-up
(needs per-OS code + a security review).

The reattach client validates the cached
credentials via `GET /v1/sessions/<id>` before
printing the welcome banner; a 401/404 drops
the saved pair and falls through to
`create_session`. The banner reads
`Re-attached to <url> (session <id>)` instead
of `Connected to <url> (session <id>)` when
reattach succeeded.

one:

1. **Server**: new `GET /v1/sessions/:id` endpoint returning a
   metadata snapshot (`session_id` + `created_at` +
   `last_eval_at` Unix timestamps + the same workspace summary

   `mlpl-repl --connect`. Both required together; either alone

   explicit flags) and writes the pair after minting a fresh
   session. Keyring-backed storage is left as a follow-up;
   the simple JSON file works on every host the REPL runs on
